summary: Positive Volume Index: a running line that moves only on bars with higher volume than the bar before, with a 255-bar EMA.
overview: The Positive Volume Index (PVI) tracks price change only on days when volume rises. It plots in its own pane with a 255-bar signal EMA.
Colors show its position against the EMA, with a gradient fill.
how: Start at 1000. On a bar with higher volume than the previous one, PVI changes by the same percent as the source (close by default). On other bars it stays the same.
The signal is a 255-bar EMA, about one trading year on daily charts. The starting value has no meaning; read the slope and the position against the EMA.
use: Some traders read PVI above its EMA as a sign of a broad uptrend.
Compare it with the Negative Volume Index.
Use it on daily charts as designed.
Watch the color change when PVI crosses its EMA.
alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.
notes: It needs volume data; on symbols without volume it shows nothing useful.
Made for daily charts; the 255-bar EMA needs a long history.
